rationale: This is a numerator swap (oancf → ebitda) on the already-archived "Loss-Runway OCF Yield" — same name, same runway ratio, and it also overlaps heavily with the archived Cash-Quality EBITDA Value, so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively new mechanism.

The only change from the archived Cash-Quality EBITDA Value (fmb 5.11, alpha 5.8%) is adding lct − che to the denominator of an already-successful filter, a denominator tweak unmotivated by any diagnosed failure and therefore a cosmetic refinement of a strong incumbent.

Structurally identical to the archived "Percentile Weakest-Link OCF Safety" with only the value anchor swapped from oancf to ebitda, so the weakest-link claim in the reasoning is not new information about the mechanism.

This is the third numerator in the same RANK(yield) × RANK(che/act) template already tested with oancf and ebitda, and ib is close enough to ebitda that little independent information is added; the stated motivation (creditor-claim denominator failure) does not justify reusing an off-the-shelf filter.

The lt/market-equity anchor is economically distinct from the earnings/cash-flow yields (a levered-value versus equity-stub test) and its prior conditioning variable failed, so pairing it with a liquid-asset survival screen is a defensible reuse of the filter rather than a pure clone — though the che/act component is well-worn and the leverage-value premium itself is close to published distress/leverage anomalies.

It simply recombines two archived components (Cash-Quality OCF Yield's che/act and the weakest-link MIN structure, with wcap/lct nearly redundant against the archived che/lct) on the same low-coverage oancf anchor, making it a mechanical permutation rather than a new economic idea.
